Compare two methods on paired study attempts

Source: R/inference_comparison.R
gt_compare_inference.Rd

Compare two methods on paired study attempts

Usage

gt_compare_inference(study, baseline, comparison)

Arguments

study

A study returned by gt_runstudy().

baseline, comparison

Distinct adapter IDs to compare explicitly.

Value

A data frame of paired counts, coverage and finite-yield differences, their Monte Carlo standard errors, and joint-finite width differences.

Details

Differences are comparison minus baseline, separately for each scenario, fixed-effect target and interval level. Every replication must occur exactly once for each method. Conditional coverage uses usable finite intervals. Finite covered-interval yield uses all scheduled attempts; a zero contribution means no usable finite covered interval, not that an unbounded confidence set excludes truth. Conditional-coverage MCSE uses paired ratio influence values. Width differences use jointly usable finite intervals. MCSEs describe asymptotic Monte Carlo uncertainty, not calibration. Matching replication keys require a study that gave methods the same data; combining unrelated studies by matching seed numbers is unsupported.

Examples

s <- gt_runstudy(gt_scenario('paired'),
  adapters = list(gt_adapter('a'), gt_adapter('b')), reps = 2L)
gt_compare_inference(s, 'a', 'b')
